workloads.description: Standard decode workload: 64 concurrent requests, 1K KV cache per request. Represents the typical online serving baseline with no memory pressure. Used as the reference point for throughput and latency regression checks.

Decode under memory pressure: 128 concurrent requests with 16K KV cache per request, intentionally exceeding GPU VRAM to trigger KV offload eviction and reload. Core scenario for validating kv-offload correctness and measuring throughput cost of offloading. Derived from the mla_decode.yaml batch spec pattern (128q1s16k) scaled to a standard attention model.

Long document Q&A: single requests with 32K–128K input tokens. Tests that KV blocks for very long sequences are correctly managed (allocated, potentially offloaded and reloaded) without corruption or silent truncation. Catches regressions in large-KV-block handling specific to the offloading path.

High prefix cache reuse: requests sharing a long common prefix (e.g., system prompt + document context). Validates that prefix blocks evicted to NVMe/CPU are correctly reloaded and hash-verified on reuse. Throughput here is sensitive to eviction policy and reload latency.

Concurrent prefill and decode: mixed batch with new requests being prefilled while existing ones are mid-decode. Exercises the scheduler's block allocation and the attention backend simultaneously. Used to detect regressions where KV offload interferes with prefill block allocation.

Agentic multi-turn workload: sequences of short decode steps interleaved with tool calls, modelling ReAct or function-calling patterns. KV blocks from earlier turns must be retained across multiple short generations. Validates that the LRU/ARC eviction policy does not prematurely evict blocks needed for active multi-turn sessions under concurrent load.

Sliding-window attention with eager SimpleCPUOffloading: requests using SlidingWindowAttention where the same physical KV block re-enters the attention window multiple times, causing the same block ID to appear more than once in the CPU offload list. Regression scenario for the KV block double-free bug (issue #42571) fixed by PR #42615. Requires SWA-enabled model and cpu_offloading enabled.

Sustained concurrent load with SimpleCPUOffloadConnector and hybrid KV cache: ~50 concurrent requests, Qwen3_5-35B-A3B model, chunked prefill enabled, large cpu_bytes_to_use. Reproduces the scheduler deadlock where Running=0 and Waiting=N with zero throughput after initial successful processing. The root cause is async KV-load requests in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS not being counted against the max_num_seqs limit (fixed by PR #42568).

Long-context requests with SimpleCPUOffloadConnector + Hybrid KV Cache Manager in sequence: first request uses a large context window saturating GPU blocks; second request triggers GPU block pool exhaustion in popleft_n (assert failure). Validates that free block accounting is correct across consecutive long-context requests with CPU offload active.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash multi-turn with repeated shared prefix: 3-step pattern A→B→A where A is the same prompt with a long shared system prompt/prefix. Repro for prefix-cache 0% hit on re-sent requests in hybrid model groups. Tests that recently-used prefix blocks are not prematurely evicted when a new request B runs between two identical requests A. Fixed by soft-pin mechanisms in PRs #42985 and #43191.

Online serving with small KV blocks requiring frequent CPU→GPU onloads: high request rate with small per-request KV footprint (4–24 KiB per descriptor). Exercises the cuMemcpyBatchAsync→Triton kernel fast path for small payload offloading. Validates that the Triton path achieves higher PCIe throughput than the DMA path for this regime (target: >20 GB/s vs. baseline 5–7 GB/s on the CPU→GPU direction).

Decode throughput regression check with CPU KV offload active: measures tokens/s during decode phase with and without CPU offload to quantify the offload overhead. Based on the regression report where LMCache CPU kv offload caused significant decode speed degradation. A >10% relative drop in output token throughput vs. no-offload baseline is a regression signal.
